techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: A malicious attachment delivered by email to obtain execution on a target host.

techniques.name: Malicious File
techniques.description: A user opens a delivered file, executing attacker-controlled content.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Legitimate credentials used to access resources, blending in with normal activity.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: PowerShell used to execute commands, frequently encoded to hinder inspection.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Command or payload content encoded to frustrate detection and review.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Command and control tunnelled over HTTP or HTTPS to blend with web traffic.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Scanning for reachable hosts and listening services inside the network.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating other hosts on the network to plan movement.

techniques.name: Password Spraying
techniques.description: A small set of passwords tried against many accounts to avoid lockout thresholds.

techniques.name: Windows Remote Management
techniques.description: WinRM used to authenticate to and execute on remote Windows hosts.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Valid accounts used with remote services to move between systems.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.description: Bulk collection from databases and repositories holding business data.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Files gathered from a compromised host prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Local Data Staging
techniques.description: Collected data consolidated into one location before removal.

techniques.name: Archive via Utility
techniques.description: A utility such as 7-Zip used to compress collected data for transfer.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Shadow copies or backups destroyed to prevent restoration after encryption.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Files encrypted in place to interrupt operations and extract payment.

techniques.name: Network Denial of Service
techniques.description: Network bandwidth or connection capacity exhausted to deny availability.
